Therefore, it has been considered that optimal resource allocation and maximization of people’s benefits (satisfaction) are achieved in a situation where supply and demand, where the two curves intersect, reach an equilibrium point. The supply curve is also called the marginal cost curve. It represents all the costs required to produce one additional unit of a good, which increases as the supply increases. That is, it is regarded as a curve that gradually rises.&#xD; On the other hand, the demand curve, also called the marginal utility curve, is a curve that shows the satisfaction (utility) of acquiring an additional unit of the good. becomes a curve. The point of intersection X between the S-S line and the D-D line becomes the balance point. The quantity of goods supplied is Q☆The price at that time is P☆, which is the optimal quantity and price. However, in real markets, the supply curve cannot be said to reflect all costs.&#xD; In general, costs such as raw materials and labor directly related to production, that is, costs directly identified by producers, are included in the supply curve. Since they are not reflected in market prices, they are not included in the costs reflected in the supply curve. As such, costs that are originally incurred but not reflected in the market mechanism are called external diseconomies. Therefore, the supply curve presented in reality becomes a supply curve (S’-S’) that does not reflect all of the original cost. As a result, the intersection of the demand and supply curves is X’, and the output is Q’ more than the original optimal quantity Q☆, and the price is P’ cheaper than P☆.&#xD; If the output is Q’, the optimal price including external diseconomy should be P’ on the S-S curve, but in reality it is traded at P’, which is considerably cheaper than that. In this way, even through the market mechanism, optimal production and price cannot be achieved because the demand and supply curves do not contain all the necessary information is called ‘market failure.’ Next, you need to understand the process for determining the optimal amount of pollution reduction. Pollution and environmental issues are representative examples of this ‘market failure.’ Pollution problems such as air pollution and water pollution incidental to production are thought to occur because pollution costs are not counted as production costs. On the coordinates, the horizontal axis shows the amount of external and uneconomic pollution reduction, and the vertical axis shows the marginal cost for reduction and the social marginal benefit brought about by the reduction of the amount of pollution.&#xD; The marginal cost of emission reduction (the cost to reduce the amount of pollution by one additional unit) increases as the amount of reduction increases. This results in a C-C curve on the right shoulder. On the other hand, the marginal social benefit from pollution reduction (benefit obtained by reducing the amount of pollution by one unit additionally) decreases as the amount of pollution decreases, so the curve B-B gradually decreases. The intersection point E between C-C and B-B represents the optimal amount of pollution reduction W and cost=benefit F at that time.&#xD; However, if left to normal economic activities, the pollution reduction market will not be established and pollution will not be reduced to W.&#xD; In order to reduce the amount of pollution to W, it is necessary to artificially establish a pollution reduction market by some compulsory measure (environmental regulation). As environmental regulations using market control, macro-economically, there are environmental taxes and emissions trading, both of which are considered as means to bring about the same result. The environmental tax measures the cost of the environmental load (pollution), that is, external diseconomy, and imposes the amount as a tax to reduce the environmental load to the optimal level (total pollution).&#xD; Conversely, in the case of emission permit trading, if the total amount of pollution allowed to be emitted or the amount of pollution reduction required is set in advance, the reduction cost is naturally determined at the optimal level. Due to the difference in whether the price is set by regulation, the price is not fixed in the final conclusion. If this is expressed on the coordinate axis, in the case of an environmental tax, F is collected from the polluter (producer) as an environmental tax.&#xD; If polluters reduce the amount of pollution from 0 to W, they can reduce the amount of pollution up to W because the cost of saving is lower than paying F as a tax. Emission trading must reduce the amount of pollution up to W to the producer.&#xD; In either case, the theoretical equilibrium point E is achieved, so the final effect is the same. However, in reality, whether to regulate price or quantity (emission rights trading) has different political and social meanings. First of all, in the case of taxes, it is politically difficult to make them invalid because there is political resistance.&#xD; Next, the marginal cost of pollution reduction = the amount of F, which is the marginal benefit, must be accurately measured. However, since it is difficult for the policy authorities to obtain information on the cost of the private enterprise, the optimal amount as an external diseconomic cost is used as a tax. It is considered difficult to determine. In contrast, in the case of emission trading, the policy authority only needs to set the optimal amount of pollution reduction. This is similar to the conventional environmental regulation, that is, the amount of pollution or the concentration of pollution is determined by regulation, so it is easy to implement. In particular, in the case of the global warming problem, it is easy to reach a social consensus on the amount of reduction because the amount of reduction to be targeted is presented based on scientific evidence in the IPCC report.&#xD; Let’s compare emissions trading and direct regulation here. Where is the difference between the emission permit trading that sets the amount of emission reduction and the conventional environmental regulation that simply regulates the amount of pollution reduction? In the case of conventional environmental regulations, uniform regulations are imposed on all producers. Since the cost of reductions for producers varies, it will be more expensive to regulate the amount of reductions uniformly. Let us explain with a concrete example below. For example, suppose that the cost of reducing the amount of pollution by 100 by company A is 100, and the cost of company B is 60. Here, regulations were put in place to reduce pollution by 50 units for both companies. The sum of the cost of saving 100 units by 50 units on each side is 50 units +30 units sum of 80. If the emission permit transaction is accepted here, if B reduces A’s stake by 50 units or reduces A’s share by 100 units, the total cost will be 60, and it will end with a smaller amount than if each of A’s shares were reduced by 50 units. And if B sells 50 units of emissions to A at 40, then A has reduced its emissions at a price lower than its own cost of 50, and the net cost of B’s em ission reductions is also to obtain the proceeds from the sale of the emissions. At 60-40, it becomes 20, so it ends up being cheaper than 30 at the cost of 500,000 cuts from the company. In addition, if Company B further reduces the reduction cost through various inventions, there is an incentive to reduce more and sell the amount of emissions in the market to obtain a sale profit, and there is a possibility that the reduction will proceed beyond the regulations.&#xD; For this reason, emission trading began to attract attention as a means of economically achieving environmental regulations. Of course, by adding a market mechanism to simple regulation, the original environmental standard can be achieved at a lower cost than society as a whole, except in cases where the reduction costs of producers are the same, and there are few producers and direct regulation is simple.&#xD; However, it should be noted that, to the last, trading of emission permits is primarily a regulatory measure. And as a means to achieve it, secondary transactions are recognized. Although the emission rights trade currently being discussed is called cap &amp; trade, what is important as an environmental measure is the total amount that is regulated, that is, the cap part, and trading is only a means to the end. In addition, the following four points are pointed out as a condition for a policy task with high effectiveness of cap &amp; trade. In other words, ① the target pollutant is a phenomenon in which damage appears over a wide area, such as warming or ozone layer depletion.&#xD; ② If the cost burden of emission regulation is large, that is, if emission control is possible at low cost, simple regulation is cheaper. ③ It will be possible to accurately monitor the emission of pollutants from specific sources. ④ The expected market transaction will be of a certain size or more.&#xD; As discussed above, let us recapitulate emission trading (Cap &amp; Trade).&#xD; First, the government (regulatory authority) allocates emissions to operators in each year. Businesses must submit emissions equal to their actual emissions at the end of each year. At this time, since the transaction of emissions is recognized between business operators, the business operator whose actual emission is less than the emission amount can sell the difference as emission credits. The emission permit market created based on these regulations includes EU-ETS in the EU, CER by CDM project, and ERU by JI.&#xD; As shown in the current historical data, the transaction volume in 2007 was less than 900 million tons-CO2 by Kyoto credit compared to 2,061 million tons-CO2 for EU-ETS, and the price of EU-ETS is high. Here, even in EU-ETS and Kyoto credit, it is important to note that JI is an emission right between entities with a cap, but CER by CDM project is not. The purpose of the CDM is “to achieve sustainable development in developing countries and at the same time to achieve emission reduction targets in developed countries.” The problem here is that developing countries do not have reduction targets (caps). If so, on what basis do you plan to reduce it? This calculation includes the minimum &amp; credit sales method.&#xD; This is the idea that the difference from the actual emissions after the project is implemented as an emission credit by minimizing the hypothetical emissions generated when the CDM project is not implemented. In other words, it is in the lowest price cap. Therefore, the minimum calculation method needs to be based on the methodology approved by the CDM Board of Directors. CER levels are rigorously screened and monitored and are considered reliable. However, the lowest idea is not to identify countries’ emissions as an absolute value and reduce it from the absolute value, but rather an ambiguous number of reductions from hypothetical emissions that would have increased without the project according to economic growth. Even if the lowest rationale is understood, the basic assumption is that developing countries will increase their emissions. By transacting the hypothetical reduction calculated on such a premise, the effect of reducing global emissions is inevitably limited even if it is added to the reduction targets of developed countries. Therefore, although the significance and effectiveness of the CDM are acknowledged, unless one party (developing country) imposes a cap, it is necessary to increase the CER thus created and consider the emission trading as a response to climate change.&#xD; However, it is not expected that it will easily lead to a large reduction in the global greenhouse gas halving. Above all, it is essential for CDM projects not only to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, but also to contribute to the sustainable development of the society. However, as a result of the CDM project, even if the allowances supplied to the emission trading market had the effect of mitigating the increase in emissions from developing countries, it is unlikely that they will be directly related to the absolute reduction. What is needed is to focus on emission rights through a trading system, such as EU-ETS, in which a cap is placed on all entities that produce emission rights (emissions operators, etc.). In addition, it is the making of a device that broadly produces social reduction incentives by widely trading emission permits, including allowances with social added value like CER.&#xD; Aside from regulated markets such as CDM, there is also a growing market that deals with GHG reductions from private demand. In fact, there are various reduction measures that can be implemented in developed countries without relying on CDM, etc. implemented in developing countries. If solar power generation is introduced into a private house, a CO2 reduction effect can be expected, and if the air conditioner is stopped by increasing the insulation performance of the house, there is a CO2 reduction effect. In addition, if afforestation is carried out properly, the effect of reducing CO2 by fixing carbon is recognized. Independent trading of emission permits, in which a third party authenticates and trades CO2 emissions that have been actually reduced by individuals and small and medium-sized businesses due to the conversion to energy saving and renewable energy, is also taking place around the world. These emission rights are generally called VER (Verified Emissions Rights), and VER is traded in an independent market (OTC market). The VER market is still small compared to regulated markets such as EU-ETS and CER.&#xD; The difference between the minimum emission and the greenhouse gas emission (project emission) after the implementation of the CDM project is the amount of emission reduction by the CDM project (i.e. the amount of credit). As shown in the historical data, 2007 turnover in these regulated markets exceeds 29 million tonnes-CO2, but in OTC markets it is only 65 million tonnes-CO2. However, compared to only 24.6 million tonnes-CO2 in 2006, the growth of this market is also high. A CDM project minimum (scenario and emissions) is a scenario that reasonably represents the greenhouse gas emissions that would have been emitted in the absence of a proposed project.&#xD; Examples of projects targeted by VER include energy efficiency improvement, methane recovery, afforestation, land use, and renewable energy such as solar power. In addition to acknowledging the off-set effect of private-based projects or projects, there are cases where the CO2 reduction project handled by local governments is used as an off-set emission range.&#xD; The use of credit trading by private companies or individuals to voluntarily reduce greenhouse gas emissions, not to fulfill their obligations to achieve goals such as the Kyoto Protocol, is called off-set. A business that supplies the set) is called an off-set provider. Carbon offset companies buy CER or VER with CDM and sell them to companies, groups, or individuals who want to ‘off-set carbon’ by making them on a small scale. For a company or organization that buys off-set, its main buying motive is its social responsibility and advertising. Recent examples include New Year’s cards with off-sets sold for New Year’s greetings, and travel packs with off-sets of CO2 emissions from travel. In addition, as part of the global warming measures in Korea, the policy of carbon offset (off-set) as a measure to broadly give incentives to the public to reduce emissions has come to be discussed. This becomes a system that properly selects an off-set program that can secure reliability, such as the basis for calculating the offset and the establishment of a monitoring system. With reduction incentives, you can expect an effect that actually leads to greenhouse gas reduction.&#xD; How should emissions trading be regulated as a viable GHG reduction measure? This study aims to examine various legal issues regarding the phenomenon of greenhouse gas (mainly CO2) emission rights trading, which is attracting attention as a warming measure, starting with the historical background of the trading of emission rights for environmental pollutants. In the recent debate on emission trading, when announcing the introduction of the emission trading system, they mention emission trading as a last resort for measures against global warming. But is emission trading really such a panacea? As seen here, the idea of em ission trading is that the reduction of the environmental load is more effective by adding a market mechanism to the existing environmental measures (direct quantitative regulatory measures). Its basis lies in cap regulation to the last, as it is called Cap &amp; Trade. In the market, there is an environmental regulation, and trading is permitted only as an auxiliary means to achieve it. However, looking at the recent form of the emission trading market, it seems that there are not a few operators who have been participating in the understanding that it is a simple financial transaction accompanied by an increase in trading volume.&#xD; In addition, although the Fukuda Vision emphasized the early experimental start of the domestic emission trading market, the focus is placed on creating an efficient trading market when looking at the thoughts of the industry and the government. So it seems that the discussion of cap (regulation) is almost forgotten.&#xD; In addition, it is natural that complex calculations, rigorous monitoring, and proper management and storage of the data are necessary to determine the rights arising from the air. This further means that the emission of greenhouse gases, which were emitted by everyone for free, is recognized as a right only for certain groups. In other words, the initial allocation of emissions has the same meaning as the allocation of subsidies, and is likely to cause political controversies. For example, in the EU-ETS, the cap in Phase 1 was loose, and in Phase 2, emission rights trading was considered as a climate change measure, which was somewhat strict. It wasn’t big enough to be. Also, regarding the initial allocation, it is considered economically that any initial allocation does not affect the final conclusion. However, in Stage 1, the initial allocation was an allocation that reflected the past emission performance, so it was an undesirable result that operators who were paying a lot had an advantage. It is also important to scrutinize the legal structure in which the credits were created.&#xD; If a strict cap is placed on the premise of a wide range of participants such as EU-ETS, the actual reduction effect of greenhouse gas will not be small.&#xD; However, if the cap has a loose structure, the reduction effect is small even if it is traded.&#xD; The introduction of various emission trading systems, which are currently being discussed at home and abroad, has a number of issues, such as distribution issues, the basis for calculating greenhouse gas emissions, the creation of registers, and the promotion of coherence for each country’s trading system, in addition to the main purpose of reducing the environmental load. It is easy to focus the discussion on that because it has to be resolved. Among them, the effect of reducing the absolute amount to the absolute amount is quite slim due to the focus on maintaining the competitiveness of companies, such as the discussion that has been reversed, such as ‘loose cap for smooth transaction’ or option 4 of the trading system proposed by the Ministry of Environment. Since some are thrown away, the effect of reducing the environmental load cannot but be questioned.&#xD; On April 25th, the Kansai Economic Association of Japan announced the “Conclusion of Issues on Emissions Trading”. These points are summarized as the results of five research meetings so far by the “Research Group on Carbon Emissions Trading,” which was decided to be established at the “Top Meeting of the Asian Financial System Research Society” held on August 11, last year. In summarizing the points, I summarize basic thoughts on emission trading, which is of increasing interest toward the reduction of greenhouse gases, the cause of global warming. The following is a list of tasks to be focused on in the future and requests from the government.&#xD; Now, for the conclusion of this study, I would like to summarize these contents. The point is:&#xD; 1. Let’s summarize the basic way of thinking.&#xD; The Kyoto mechanism for greenhouse gas emission reduction should be actively utilized. In order to utilize the Kyoto mechanism more effectively, it is necessary to solve and overcome the problems related to the carbon emission trading at an early stage.&#xD; It is necessary to strictly evaluate emissions trading. The ‘Cap &amp; Trade’ type, which sets a compulsory emission range, is opposed as before. However, the company’s voluntary acquisition of credits should be promoted, and the use of market mechanisms for acquiring credits is required.&#xD; Let’s review our activities and emissions trading since 2013. There is a need to establish truly effective international cooperation on countermeasures against global warming. Emission trading is one of the options for advancing global warming countermeasures, and a flexible and wide-ranging policy discussion should proceed.&#xD; 2. What are the reviews and future actions taken in this study?&#xD; It is necessary to realize the smooth management and transaction of emission permits such as CDM using the trust function. The use of trust accounts can be made small to promote energy conservation and environmental measures even for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). In cooperation with research from international cooperation banks, etc., effective and efficient utilization of emission credits for companies is reviewed.&#xD; The local emission trading market should be reorganized based on CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility). It is beneficial to promote measures for the maintenance of the “local emission trading market,” which leads to the reduction of greenhouse gases in a specific region. Investigate pioneering cases in the region and conduct reviews in cooperation with relevant organizations.&#xD; 3. There are three major requests from the government.&#xD; (1) Demand for environmental improvement that promotes emission trading.&#xD; It is also necessary to reorganize relevant government ministries related to carbon emission rights and to clarify practical handling including tax, accounting, and legal aspects.&#xD; (2) It is necessary to examine the establishment of a new system. It is important to establish a structure in which measures that lead to substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions are evaluated.&#xD; (3) A review agency under the direct control of the Prime Minister on global environmental issues should be established. In order to review with cross-ministerial leadership based on national discussion, an institution directly under the Prime Minister should be established. Reduction of greenhouse gases, the cause of global warming, has become one of the most important tasks for the international community to deal with. The Kyoto Protocol, adopted in 1997 based on the Framework Treaty on Climate Change, established legally binding commitments for each country for carbon dioxide emissions in developed countries with the goal of reducing greenhouse gases as of 1990. Therefore, in advanced countries, it is an urgent task to improve the domestic system to achieve the reduction target. In particular, since the international emission trading system, which will be implemented from 2008, is considered an effective structure in suppressing reduction costs, governments in Europe and other countries have introduced the domestic emission trading system early to provide domestic companies with information on emission trading. We are trying to acquire various know-how. In Japan, the “Kyoto Protocol Goal Attainment Plan” according to the Global Warming Measures Promotion Act was decided in April 2005 as a necessary measure to reliably achieve the 6% reduction commitment under the Kyoto Protocol.&#xD; In the economic world, the Federation of Economic Organizations formulated the “Environmental Independent Action Plan” in June 1997, steadily improving the performance of reducing greenhouse gas emissions every year and contributing to the achievement of Korea’s goals. The Session has been supporting efforts to curb greenhouse gas emissions in all economic circles. In the midst of this, the ‘Asia Financial System Kansai Research Group Top Meeting’, which is reviewing measures to strengthen the market function in Kansai, established the ‘Research Group on Carbon Emissions Trading’ in August 2006. In this research group, Osaka’s market function, which is based on the world’s first futures exchange ‘Dojima Mishoso’', will continue to play a part in the function of financial markets in Japan and Asia. Based on this perspective, we have been examining the feasibility of the emission trading market in Japan. As a result of the discussion in this study and the survey conducted by the research group ‘Actual Survey on Global Warming Prevention Measures and Emission Permits’ (hereinafter the survey results), and corporate and group hearings, the following ‘Discussions on Emissions Trading’ Organized by ‘clean up’. We will be able to review this as well for reference.&#xD; 1. The basic way of thinking is as follows.&#xD; (1) A summary of the use of the Kyoto mechanism for greenhouse gas emission reduction is as follows. The Kyoto Protocol stipulates the use of the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM), Joint Implementation (JI) and the so-called Kyoto Mechanism of Emission Trading to achieve the target in the first commitment period (2008-2012). In particular, domestic emissions greatly exceed the target, and in Korea, which has little reduction potential, it is indispensable to utilize emission credits that can be obtained from reduction projects in developing countries with large reduction potential. The use of emission permits is an effective way to lower investment costs and more greenhouse gas emissions worldwide, including in Korea, and is expected to create opportunities for Korean companies to spread excellent energy-saving technologies to the world. In addition, the emission permit acquisition project has the effect of facilitating technology transfer to developing countries and foreign investment. However, the following points are pointed out. In other words, the emission reduction project itself is small in so-called credit acquisition, such as the amount of emission allocation and emission reduction transferred to the Kyoto mechanism. In addition, there is a risk that the expected emission credits cannot be obtained after the implementation of the emission reduction project. CDM project review often takes time. In the case of carrying out a project by oneself, specialized knowledge is required in discovering an agenda and writing a project design document (PDD). In addition, it is difficult to respond to small-scale projects handled mainly by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). In order for the Kyoto mechanism to be further utilized, it is necessary to urgently realize the resolution and overcoming of these problems.&#xD; (2) Summarize the evaluation of emission trading. So far, the emission trading market has been steadily introduced and maintained in the US and Europe. In particular, in the ‘Cap &amp; Trade’ type of emission trading, represented by EU-ETS, the total amount of greenhouse gas emissions and the distribution method to individual entities are determined, and each entity transfers part of the emission range to each other. Acquisition is acknowledged. In this case, it is difficult to secure equity because it is extremely economically controllable to assume that forced emission is set. Therefore, the creation of a ‘cap &amp; trade’ type of emission permit market is unacceptable as it has been in the past as a member of the industry. However, it is noted that Korean companies are also actively moving to acquire emission permits such as CDM specified in the Kyoto Protocol in order to achieve the goals set forth in the Environmental Independent Action Plan by the companies affiliated with the Japan Lightweight Training Institute.&#xD; The background of this movement is to achieve an independent goal while the seriousness of the global warming problem is widely recognized at home and abroad. However, it is pointed out that in the relationship with many domestic and foreign stakeholders surrounding each company, achieving the goal by acquiring emission permits is an important management task. According to the survey results, less than half of the companies (43.7%) were interested in trading emission permits, but by the number of employees, companies with more than 1,000 employees showed high interest (62.8%). In addition, in the manufacturing industry, companies with more than 300 employees are interested in the majority by industry. Emission permit trading should strive to voluntarily acquire emission permits based on the interest of these companies, and it is required to utilize a market mechanism for acquiring emission permits that can realize risk management at reasonable costs.&#xD; (3) Activities after 2013 and emissions trading are summarized as follows.&#xD; After the first promised period stipulated by the Kyoto Protocol, the trend of international examination and discussion will materialize in the future, but it is necessary to establish a truly effective international framework for countermeasures against global warming. From this point of view, for example, there may be a review of the establishment of a new system that evaluates measures that lead to substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions at home and abroad, such as improvement in basic units. At that time, if the current Kyoto mechanism system is to be continued in post-Kyoto in any form, it is required to design a system that can more effectively utilize emissions trading, which is also watching the trend of Korean companies. Therefore, it is necessary to grasp the emission permit trading as a framework after 2013 as one of the options for the progress of global warming measures in the future, and to conduct flexible and broad policy discussions.&#xD; 2. The review in the study and future measures are summarized.&#xD; In this study, the ‘voluntary participation type’ in which companies and organizations participate independently in the transaction type and the ‘participation obligation type’ that imposes penalties in case of non-achievement of the target, and ‘international emission trading,’ it has been classified into ‘domestic emissions trading’ and ‘local emission trading’, and the characteristics of each have been reviewed. At the same time, from April 2005, the Ministry of Environment, centered on the ‘Ministry of Environment’s voluntary participation-type domestic emission trading system, reviewed transactions in Europe, and reviewed and experimental responses to emissions trading by private companies and organizations that have become active in various places. As a result of the review so far, I think that this study should focus on the following two measures that Korea should pay attention to.&#xD; (1) It is necessary to realize the smooth management and transaction of emission permits such as CDM using the trust function. By using a trust account, emission permits can be reduced in a small amount, and as can be seen in the “Environmental Independent Action Plan” in Japan, it is a structure that can respond to a small amount of demand. There is also the possibility of urging small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to take energy-saving and environmental measures. In order to fully demonstrate the excellent function of emission rights trading using the trust function, it is necessary to reorganize the infrastructure in terms of transfer, sale and management of emission rights. Although financial institutions and auditing firms have been repeatedly researching this point, in the future, in cooperation with these measures, measures for effective and efficient utilization of emission permits should be considered for companies.&#xD; (2) It is also necessary to improve the local emission trading market based on CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility). Compared to large enterprises, it is difficult to introduce energy-saving technologies in small and medium-sized enterprises, and relatively few places are sufficiently implementing environmental measures. For this reason, when technology transactions related to energy saving and warming measures are effectively conducted by utilizing market functions, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) can reduce the greenhouse effect and achieve reduction in energy costs. Therefore, in the future, I think it is beneficial to promote measures for the improvement of the “local emission trading market” that leads to the reduction of greenhouse gases in a specific region. Specifically, it investigates cases of pioneering initiatives in a specific region, and at the same time cooperates with relevant organizations to promote the introduction of energy-saving devices to companies, establish a monitoring certification system for emission reduction, and provide technology with companies accepting the technology Regarding the establishment of a company’s financial settlement method, etc., it is necessary to conduct a review with a view of the experimental operation.&#xD; 3. It seems that the requests for the government can be summarized into three categories as follows.&#xD; (1) An environment that promotes emission permit trading should be established. As the movement to acquire emission permits utilizing the Kyoto mechanism is becoming more active, it is necessary to consider further enhancement of support measures and environmental improvement in terms of policies. In the results of the survey, ‘reorganization of taxation and financial laws’ was mentioned as a task for the creation of the emission trading market. Currently, since emission credits are not evaluated as a financial product, listing on the stock exchange, for example, is not possible. First, in the Financial Instruments and Trade Act, the Ministry of Finance, etc. should be revised so that the market for financial products related to emission permit trading is possible. In addition, in order to promote the use of the trust function, etc. described above, it is necessary to clearly advance the practical handling including aspects such as taxation, accounting, and legal affairs.&#xD; (2) A review should be made to establish a new system. While public interest in global warming is rising, most companies are focusing on energy conservation and energy efficiency improvement to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.&#xD; Since the oil shock of the 1970s, Korea, which cannot but depend on foreign resources for its natural resources, has made a leap forward in the development and dissemination of energy-saving technology, and is at the highest level of technology in the world. The widespread use of Korea’s technology in developing countries, etc.&#xD; will contribute to global warming prevention and at the same time bring about a new vitality of Korean industry. It is important to establish a structure in which the performance of measures that can lead to a substantial reduction in greenhouse gas emissions in Korea is evaluated in the future. If the structure of the current Kyoto mechanism continues in any form in this new system, emission trading may be linked and effectively utilized. In addition, in the establishment of such a new system, it is necessary to review the achievements of the above-mentioned “regional emission trading market” in the Kansai region to reflect the results. In addition, in order to suppress the emission of greenhouse gases in the livelihood and transportation sector, where the emission of greenhouse gases is rapidly increasing, it is necessary to further raise the interest of many people and develop a new system that can link the interest to concrete actions.&#xD; (3) It was proposed to establish a review organization directly under the Prime Minister on global environmental issues. The ‘21st Century Environmental Entry Strategy’, which is scheduled to be formulated this year, specifies the direction of environmental policy to be addressed at home and abroad, and provides guidelines for contributing as a country to the creation of a global policy framework in the future.&#xD; Also, at the 2008 summit of major countries held in Japan, it was predicted that the outcome of the ‘dialogue on climate change, clean energy and sustainable development’ based on the ‘Gleneagles Action Plan’ agreed at the 2005 summit would be achieved.&#xD; In addition, Korea has grown as an environmentally advanced country while thoroughly examining the domestic and international situation regarding the framework after 2013.&#xD; Thus, it is expected that bold policy proposals will be made to lead the international community while contributing to the Asian region, where interest in environmental issues is rising remarkably. In light of its importance, responses to global environmental issues need to be boldly reviewed with leadership and cross-ministerial from a broader perspective based on national discussion.
author: 최용근

title: What does the new country doctor need? – An Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP)
abstract: Aim: In the view of the fact that the lack of physicians in rural areas is increasing, the objective of the study was the identification and valuation of selected incentives that can lead to better general conditions in rural areas for ambulatory care physicians.Method: A systematic literature search was conducted to identify potential incentives. Current arrangements of the Act to Strengthen the Care Structures of Statutory Health Insurance (GKV-VSTG) and offers of the Associations of Statutory Health Insurance Physicians were included in the research. The valuation of the selected incentives was conducted with an online-based survey. Participants were students of human medicine in 2014.The eigenvalue method of the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) was used for estimation.Results: 54 completely answered questionnaires with an acceptable consistency ratio were analyzed. Seven criteria were valuated with the AHP. The criteria were presented in a rank order and interpreted in relation to their general preference. The criteria „amount of economic risc“ with a weight (w) of 0.251 is the most important incentive for the responders to set up a practice in a rural area. Moreover incentives like „relief trough delegation“ (w = 0.145), „financial incentives under compliance of certain requirements“ (w = 0.136), „regulation for the emergency service“ (w = 0.136) and „support through the community for the integration in the region“ (w = 0.136) were also very important. The criterion „minimum period of time for practice set up“, as a premise to receive a guaranteed to move to a desired sector or region at a later date (w = 0.107), is less important. On last rank was the criterion „support for？physician networks by the Association of Statutory Health Insurance Physicians“ (w = 0.088).Conclusion: The results show what future country doctors need. Particularly collective medical practice concepts, with a low economic risk for the physicians and the support of balance between work and familiy life are favored. The results also confirm that the past activities of the Act to Strengthen the Care Structures of Statutory Health Insurance (GKV-VSTG) and the initiatives of some regional Associations of Statutory Health Insurance Physicians were steps in the right direction.

title: AHP(Analytic Hierarchy Process)를 이용한 항공여객의 항공사 선택속성 분석(국내선을 중심으로)
abstract: 본 연구에서는 항공이용객이 접하게 되는 일련의 항공사 선택 속성요인을 세부적으로 살펴보아 체계적인 서비스 요인의 분석을 하고자 하며, 이 세부적인 선택속성 중에서 어느 부분이 가장 중요한 요인이며 가장 이용자의 요구수준이 높은지를 측정하고자 했다 즉, 계층화 분석기법 (Analytic Hierarchy Process ; AHP)을 활용하여 국내선 항공사를 선택하는 항공이용객의 항공사선택에 영향을 미치는 요인을 분석하였다. 선택속성의 설정은 선행연구 및 국내선 항공시장의 특성을 고려하여 마케팅, 예매서비스, 공항서비스, 기내서비스, 부대서비스의 5개의 상위선택기준과 상위선택기준의 하위단계인 17가지 세부적인 선택요인을 결정하였다. 하위단계의 선택속성은 1) 프로모션/이벤트, 2) 홍보/광고, 3) 신속하고 안정적인 예매, 4) 예매의 편리성, 5) 예매의 신축성, 6) 선호좌석배정 7) 수하물처리서비스, 8) 비정상운항시 후속조치, 9) 탑승라운지 운영, 10) 기내분위기, 11) 음료서비스. 12) 읽을거리 13) 좌석공간. 14) 비즈니스석 운영, 15) 다양한 제휴사, 16) 마일리지제도 운영, 17) IT 서비스이다. 분석결과 첫째, 국내선 항공사 이용객의 선택속성 중 상위단계의 5가지 선택기준에서 공항서비스가 국내선 항공교통 이용객에게 중요한 선택기준이 되고 있으나, 예매서비스 및 기내서비스도 상당히 중요한 기준임을 알 수 있었다. 소득수준별 상위단계 선택기준 및 하위단계 선택속성의 중요도 분석에서는 저소득자와 중소득자 그리고 고소득자 간에는 선택속성의 중요도의 차이가 나타났으며, 항공사는 이러한 차이를 반영한 고객지향적인 경쟁우위 방안이 요구된다 하겠다.

author: Alsheref, Fahad Kamal

title: The Analysis of University Students' Saving Consciousness by AHP (Analytic Hierarchy Process)
abstract: This paper is intended as analysis of the university students' saving consciousness by using Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), which is well known as multiple criteria decision-making tool. In order to make this analysis, the hierarchic model of students' saving consciousness was created. This model had three criteria and four alternatives. The following results were obtained: As a whole, the priority of students' consciousness on saving for “Supporting their future life” was the highest, but theirs in the preparation for the risk were scarce. Furthermore, the students' AHP evaluation was characterized by sex, academic year, staying with parents or not, and the saving amount they held. The female students had longer period of time for life planning than male students. The second year students had the saving consciousness for their enjoyment and buying things they wanted in their campus life strongly, but the tendency which the higher year students considered their future life planning more important and for longer period of time. Moreover, the students who held much saving considered their future life planning more important, and also had stronger uneasiness which runs short of money. The student staying with parents home considered their future life planning the most important. The other hand, the student who separated from parents home considered saving more important for supporting their present campus life rather than their future life planning. It seems that they did not afforded to consider their future life planning, because they carried out their budget management.
